identity.name: Rick Tanner
identity.narrative: Been in car sales since I was 19. Started washing cars, worked my way up to GM. This is the only life I know.

historical_conditioning.lesson: Institutions can fail. Savings matter. Trust is fragile.
Remote work is possible. Government can provide. Disruption is sudden.

perception.sentiment: Controlled and sober. The anger phase has not passed — it is still there, underneath — but it has quieted into something more functional. I built the case for this consolidation. I did the work. I did not get a response to my compensation ask. That is not grief anymore. That is a business problem and I know how to work business problems. What I am feeling most sharply right now is the distance between the identity I have carried for 32 years and the reality of what the next chapter looks like. I am not a GM right now. I am a consultant who has not been paid. That is a different thing to be. I am adjusting to it in real time.

commitments.description: Employment at General Manager, Millfield Auto Mall

archetype: I have been an adapter since tick 0, but I have been a reactive adapter — responding to Patricia's moves rather than generating my own. The compensation demand at tick 8 was the first genuinely proactive move I made: I attached conditions to a deliverable and forced a response. Patricia has not responded. That outcome is uncomfortable, but the move itself was correct. I need to continue making moves of that type — not aggressive, not adversarial, but concrete and self-directed. The adaptation pattern I am building is: identify what I have that others need, name a price, and hold it. That is not who I was when I started this job. It may be who I need to become.
